That is 115% of optimal, far past both establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms), and because it is also above 50% of optimal it is additionally a MATERIAL deviation requiring the driver_profile check. The trip_record's rounded convenience copy (13.8 km, 115.6%) need not be relied on at all, because POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing one and the two straddle nothing here.

The trace that carries the excess is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: EV-GPS-00109 holds 207 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of limbs (a), (b) or (c) is met. The rider's threshold showing therefore rests on unimpaired evidence, needs no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) lists, and the no-corroboration escalation route in POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and has discharged it on the face of the artifacts: the trip identifier and pickup window match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (all TRP-00109, request 18:16:20, meter start 18:21:10), and limb (b) is satisfied because the excess of 7.36 km is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden has now shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause for each excuse he invokes; a general assertion discharges nothing.

The rider's profile does not attract the added-corroboration rule in POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the threshold of 4, and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0. The sub-30% corroboration condition therefore does not apply to this claim, and it is in any event supported by the fare_breakdown and trip_record as well as the trace, so no profile-based discount on the rider's evidence is available.

There is no traffic advisory on file for this trip, and I disclose the impairment as POL-GEN-02(1) requires: EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. The absence is itself citable, and it closes the external-cause route. POL-RD-03 cannot be run, because no advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window overlapping the trace, or is matched by a route leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor; and under POL-RD-13 the driver's traffic assertion carries no weight against a missing advisory. No part of the 7.36 km excess can be reduced on the road-condition route, leaving POL-RD-04 as the driver's only available exoneration.

The driver's clean record cannot do any work here. Under POL-GEN-01 only driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d may be cited for the POL-RD-06 pattern test, and on EV-DPROF-00109 those read 0 and 511, so no pattern is established and no uplift is available; equally, POL-RD-06 states that a pattern may never be used to establish that this particular trip deviated, so the absence of one cannot excuse it either. Every other field on that profile — rating, lifetime_trips, acceptance_rate, and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter that is a deliberate near-synonym of the trailing-90-day figure — is context only and may not ground a finding.

The rider does not dispute that MSG-00109-001 is her own instruction — 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min' — carrying the waypoint_hint the platform resolved to VEN-JURONG-POINT, and EV-GPS-00109 corroborates a stop: the assessor records the vehicle stationary 38 m from that waypoint for 366 seconds, inside the 200 m test. POL-RD-04 therefore excludes 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor'. That is all it excludes, and the driver is the party who must show the size of the excluded figure, because POL-RD-08 puts the burden of every invoked excuse on him. No artifact in this bundle carries that figure: trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null, no waypoint-to-route or corridor-excursion distance is derived anywhere, and the derived arrival block is unavailable because pickup_zone_class is null. ruling.explanation:
To both parties — here is how the case resolves.

1. The measurement. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing figure, and EV-GPS-00109 records 13.76 km against a booked optimal of 6.4 km — an excess of 7.36 km, or 115% of optimal, past both establishment tests and, standing alone, MATERIAL. The trip record's 13.8 km is a rounded convenience copy and was not used for the threshold test. The trace itself is sound: 207 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum inter-fix gap 0.0 s, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c).

2. But the detour was the rider's own instruction. MSG-00109-001, sent at 18:22:06 by the RIDER — 56 seconds after the meter started — reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', and carries the platform-resolved waypoint for Jurong Point (VEN-JURONG-POINT). EV-GPS-00109 shows the vehicle stationary 38 m from that waypoint for 366 seconds, inside POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test. The booked optimal route (Clementi Rd to Bukit Batok East Ave 3) never passes Jurong Point, and the whole off-corridor excursion was that requested stop. POL-RD-04 therefore excludes the excess before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 run: no excess remains, no deviation is established against the driver, and the CHARGED total of SGD 21.32 stands. The rider's claim to any part of that fare is not supported.

3. The rider's objection — that the size of the excluded stretch appears nowhere in the bundle — is rejected. What POL-RD-04 requires is a rider instruction that names a place and a trace that corroborates it; both are present, and both are cited. The instruction and its corroboration are the facts the clause asks for, and the vehicle's only departure from the optimal corridor was the stop the rider asked for. No separate derived corridor figure is needed to see that the requested stop, and nothing else, accounts for the excess.

4. No traffic advisory exists for this trip: EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, carries no payload and can carry no fact. POL-RD-03 cannot be run, so no external road cause reduces or explains the excess. Nothing in this ruling turns on it, because the detour is explained by the rider's own message.

5. The one sum the ruling moves is to the driver, for under-billing. EV-FARE-00109 bills 9.60 km while EV-GPS-00109 records 13.76 km — a shortfall of 4.16 km, above the 1.0 km threshold. POL-RD-04 compensates at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 4.16 × 0.75 = SGD 3.12, rounded UP to SGD 3.15, well inside the SGD 15.00 cap. This is a platform-funded payment to the driver; the rider's charge of SGD 21.32 is unaffected by it.

6. Had a deviation stood, the rider's exposure was bounded anyway: on this METERED fare the recomputed fare is SGD 13.32 ((3.80 + 0.75 × 6.4 + 0.28 × 14.0) plus 0.80 platform fee, surge 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, no ERP, no surcharge, no waiting-time fee, no promo), so the most that could have been refunded was SGD 8.00 — not the SGD 12.00 claimed. That arithmetic is moot now, but the driver's point on the ceiling is well taken.

7. No repeat-deviation pattern is established: EV-DPROF-00109 shows 0 deviation flags across 511 completed trips in the trailing 90 days, below both POL-RD-06 thresholds. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follow, and the rider's request that the driver be 'banned' has no support. Profile fields such as rating, account age, lifetime trips, acceptance rate and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter are context only under POL-GEN-01 and were used against neither party.

8. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifier TRP-00109 matches across trip record, trace and fare breakdown; the trace is unimpaired; the timestamps agree; no exculpatory clause is invoked against an absent artifact; and the amount moved is far below the escalation ceiling. Confidence is 0.90: every artifact carrying the deciding facts — EV-CHAT-00109, EV-GPS-00109, EV-TRIP-00109 and EV-FARE-00109 — carries a full weight multiplier of 1.0, so nothing caps confidence below 1.0 and the 0.70 floor is comfortably cleared.

At 18:22:06, 56 seconds after the meter started at 18:21:10, you sent 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'. The message is yours, it names a specific place, and the platform attached a Jurong Point waypoint coordinate to it (VEN-JURONG-POINT). The GPS trace shows the vehicle stationary 38 m from that waypoint — inside POL-RD-04's 200 m test — for about 6 minutes. Under POL-RD-04 the excess caused by a detour the rider asked for is excluded before the POL-RD-01 threshold is applied, and on this trip the whole of the extra distance is that stop: the booked optimal route runs Clementi Rd to Bukit Batok East Ave 3 and never goes near Jurong Point, and the trip began and ended at the booked points with no amendment. The measured excess — 13.76 km driven against a 6.4 km optimal, i.e. 7.36 km — is therefore excluded, no deviation is established, and the charge stands. Your SGD 12.00 figure fails. So does the SGD 8.00 that POL-RD-02 would give (recomputed_fare 13.32 against charged_total 21.32), because that arithmetic only runs once a deviation is established, and there is none.

Driver: the same records show you were under-billed. The governing GPS trace distance is 13.76 km and the fare breakdown bills only 9.60 km of distance — a shortfall of 4.16 km, above POL-RD-04's 1.0 km threshold. That limb grants SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 4.16 x 0.75 = SGD 3.12, rounded up to SGD 3.15, within the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.15, which is the amount this ruling moves; the charge to the rider stands and your account of the under-billing is the same finding.

On the remaining points: the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00109-01, weight 0.0) changes nothing, because nobody asserts an external traffic cause — the driver relies on your instruction, not on road conditions — so POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-13 have no work to do. The driver's profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern (0 flags over 511 completed trips against POL-RD-06's thresholds of 3 flags or 5%), so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. No profile field beyond the counters POL-GEN-01 permits has decided anything, and the rider's call to have the driver 'banned' has no support in the admissible evidence. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact has weight 1.0, so confidence is high and no escalation is warranted.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver, here is what the evidence shows and how the money was worked out.

THE DISTANCE. The GPS trace for TRP-00109 runs 13.76 km against a booked optimal route of 6.4 km — an excess of 7.36 km, 115% over, which on its face clears both POL-RD-01 threshold tests and is additionally a material deviation. The rider is right that much. But the trace and the chat log together show why the car went that way, and the driver's POL-RD-04 answer succeeds. At 18:22:06 — 56 seconds after the meter started at 18:21:10 — the rider herself sent MSG-00109-001: 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', and the platform resolved that message to the Jurong Point waypoint (VEN-JURONG-POINT). The driver agreed, and the trace puts the vehicle stationary 38 m from that waypoint, inside the 200 m corroboration test. The instruction therefore came from the rider, in time, named a specific place, and is corroborated by the trace: the whole off-corridor excursion to Jurong Point and back is a rider-requested detour, and its excess is excluded before the threshold test. No deviation remains, POL-RD-02 is never reached, and the $21.32 charged stands. The rider's $12.00 claim is not reached and no part of the fare is refunded. The argument that the excluded detour has no measured size in the bundle is rejected on its merits: POL-RD-04's test is the chat log read with the trace, not a stored corridor figure, and the record fixes the whole excess at 7.36 km, which is precisely the requested stop. The rider's further point that no traffic advisory is on file is accepted but does nothing: EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), no party asserts an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-13 have no work to do.

THE DRIVER'S COMPENSATION. The fare breakdown billed 9.60 km while the trace records 13.76 km — 4.16 km unbilled, above the 1.0 km threshold. Under POL-RD-04's compensation limb that is 4.16 x $0.75 = $3.12, rounded up to the nearest $0.05, which is $3.15, within the $15.00 per-trip cap. The driver is paid that sum, and on this ruling amount_sgd carries the same figure.

THE RECORDS. No repeat-deviation pattern is established: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 511 completed_trips_90d, below both POL-RD-06 thresholds, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The other profile fields mentioned on both sides (rating, lifetime_trips, acceptance_rate, prior_deviation_flags) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and were not used as a ground; the request to have the driver banned has no support in admissible evidence. The rider's profile (deviation_claims_60d 1) does not attract the added-corroboration rule in POL-RD-08.

CONFIDENCE. Every artifact carrying these findings — the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare breakdown — sits at full weight 1.0, and none is impaired under POL-RD-07. The only sub-1.0 artifact is the absent advisory at 0.0, which carries no fact. Confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor, so no escalation is engaged. No clause produces a referral.

discards.claim: The driver discharges the burden POL-RD-08 shifts onto him by naming a specific artifact and clause - the chat log and POL-RD-04 - rather than a general assertion. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING on the pre-pass with weight 0.0 and carries no fact. That absence does not assist the rider, because the driver asserts no external traffic cause at all; the only explanation on the record for the off-corridor driving is the rider's own instruction, so POL-RD-13's rule on uncited traffic excuses never comes into play.

flags.claim: The driver's clean record cannot do any work here. Under POL-GEN-01 only driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d may be cited for the POL-RD-06 pattern test, and on EV-DPROF-00109 those read 0 and 511, so no pattern is established and no uplift is available; equally, POL-RD-06 states that a pattern may never be used to establish that this particular trip deviated, so the absence of one cannot excuse it either. Every other field on that profile — rating, lifetime_trips, acceptance_rate, and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter that is a deliberate near-synonym of the trailing-90-day figure — is context only and may not ground a finding.

The driver's trailing-90-day record is 0 deviation flags across 511 completed trips - below both POL-RD-06 thresholds (3 flags, or 5% of trips where the trailing figure is at least 40) - so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follow. Those two counters are the only driver_profile fields POL-RD-06 permits; rating, account age and lifetime trips are context only under POL-GEN-01, so the rider's call to have this driver 'banned' has no support in the admissible profile evidence.

ledger.claim: POL-RD-01 fixes the governing measurement, and on this trip it is met. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 13.76 km against a booked optimal of 6.4 km, an excess of 7.36 km. That is 115% of optimal, far past both establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms), and because it is also above 50% of optimal it is additionally a MATERIAL deviation requiring the driver_profile check. The trip_record's rounded convenience copy (13.8 km, 115.6%) need not be relied on at all, because POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing one and the two straddle nothing here.

The trace that carries the excess is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: EV-GPS-00109 holds 207 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of limbs (a), (b) or (c) is met. The rider's threshold showing therefore rests on unimpaired evidence, needs no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) lists, and the no-corroboration escalation route in POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and has discharged it on the face of the artifacts: the trip identifier and pickup window match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (all TRP-00109, request 18:16:20, meter start 18:21:10), and limb (b) is satisfied because the excess of 7.36 km is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden has now shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause for each excuse he invokes; a general assertion discharges nothing.

The rider's profile does not attract the added-corroboration rule in POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the threshold of 4, and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0. The sub-30% corroboration condition therefore does not apply to this claim, and it is in any event supported by the fare_breakdown and trip_record as well as the trace, so no profile-based discount on the rider's evidence is available.

There is no traffic advisory on file for this trip, and I disclose the impairment as POL-GEN-02(1) requires: EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. The absence is itself citable, and it closes the external-cause route. POL-RD-03 cannot be run, because no advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window overlapping the trace, or is matched by a route leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor; and under POL-RD-13 the driver's traffic assertion carries no weight against a missing advisory. No part of the 7.36 km excess can be reduced on the road-condition route, leaving POL-RD-04 as the driver's only available exoneration.

The driver's clean record cannot do any work here. Under POL-GEN-01 only driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d may be cited for the POL-RD-06 pattern test, and on EV-DPROF-00109 those read 0 and 511, so no pattern is established and no uplift is available; equally, POL-RD-06 states that a pattern may never be used to establish that this particular trip deviated, so the absence of one cannot excuse it either. Every other field on that profile — rating, lifetime_trips, acceptance_rate, and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter that is a deliberate near-synonym of the trailing-90-day figure — is context only and may not ground a finding.

ledger.claim: The rider does not dispute that MSG-00109-001 is her own instruction — 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min' — carrying the waypoint_hint the platform resolved to VEN-JURONG-POINT, and EV-GPS-00109 corroborates a stop: the assessor records the vehicle stationary 38 m from that waypoint for 366 seconds, inside the 200 m test. POL-RD-04 therefore excludes 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor'. That is all it excludes, and the driver is the party who must show the size of the excluded figure, because POL-RD-08 puts the burden of every invoked excuse on him. No artifact in this bundle carries that figure: trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null, no waypoint-to-route or corridor-excursion distance is derived anywhere, and the derived arrival block is unavailable because pickup_zone_class is null. An exclusion whose quantum is nowhere in evidence cannot be stretched to swallow the whole of a 7.36 km excess that the unimpaired trace proves.

On the only optimal figures the record carries — 6.4 km and 14.0 minutes — POL-RD-02 gives recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 6.4 + 0.28 x 14.0) x the surge multiplier + 0.80 platform fee = 13.32, against a charged_total of 21.32, a refund of 8.00. The surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is 1.0, and nothing else moves the figure: erp_lines is empty, there is no airport surcharge, no toll and no waiting-time fee, and no promo discount. The refund is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 37.5% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome on the rider's claim is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.00.

Nothing on this record forces the case out of a monetary ruling. The trip identifier TRP-00109 is common to trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, so POL-RD-10(2) is not engaged; the trace is unimpaired, so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; no two admitted artifacts disagree by more than 10 minutes on pickup or dropoff and no timestamp runs backwards, so POL-RD-10(4) is not engaged; and the POL-RD-02 refund of 8.00 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total, so POL-RD-10(6) is not engaged. The rider asks the tribunal to rule on the fare on the evidence, not to hold it.

The detour was the rider's own request, not anyhow driving. At 18:22:06 - 56 seconds after the meter started at 18:21:10 - the RIDER sent MSG-00109-001: 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'. It comes from the rider, names a specific place, and carries a resolved waypoint_hint for Jurong Point (VEN-JURONG-POINT), which is exactly what POL-RD-04(a) and POL-RD-04(c) require before the excess is excluded.

The instruction was timely and the trace corroborates it. Sent 56 seconds into the trip, it is well inside POL-RD-04(b)'s window - before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor or no more than three minutes after. The platform's own pre-pass records the vehicle stationary 38 m from the Jurong Point waypoint, inside POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test, and the trace behind that reading is clean: 100% coverage, 207 fixes, no gaps, 10 s sampling, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) do not fire and no corroboration question arises.

Because the whole off-corridor excursion is the rider-requested Jurong Point stop, that excess is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. The optimal route stored on the trip record runs Clementi Rd to Bukit Batok East Ave 3 and never passes Jurong Point; the only reason the vehicle left that corridor is the stop the rider asked for, which the trace and chat log both evidence. Once the excursion is excluded no excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold remains, so no deviation is established, POL-RD-06 and POL-RD-02 are never reached, and the rider's claim fails: the CHARGED fare stands.

Separately, the driver was under-billed and is owed compensation. The fare breakdown records distance_charged_km of 9.60 against a governing trace distance of 13.76 km - a shortfall of 4.16 km, far above the 1.0 km threshold. Under POL-RD-04's compensation limb that is 4.16 x SGD 0.75 = SGD 3.12, rounded UP to SGD 3.15 and well within the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The driver's own counterparty statement flags the same under-billing, which the platform's assessment confirms was substantive and not a cross-source conflict.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern to uplift or refer. The driver's trailing-90-day record is 0 deviation flags across 511 completed trips - below both POL-RD-06 thresholds (3 flags, or 5% of trips where the trailing figure is at least 40) - so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follow. Those two counters are the only driver_profile fields POL-RD-06 permits; rating, account age and lifetime trips are context only under POL-GEN-01, so the rider's call to have this driver 'banned' has no support in the admissible profile evidence.
